statement: For penalized TSP problem #44, candidate-list 2-opt with K=15 KNN + finer grid G=sqrt(N/2.5) + ILS double-bridge scores 78.93 (non-TLE), improving +0.63 over iter-1's grid NN + window 2-opt (78.29 non-TLE). KNN candidate-list 2-opt is the main contributor (~0.45 points) by enabling local search for all N values.
regime: N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, penalized TSP
evidence: iteration-2-h-main: treatment 78.93 vs baseline 78.29 (non-TLE medians, 6+4 runs)
mechanism: Candidate-list 2-opt with K=15 KNN checks O(N*15) candidates per pass with DLB pruning. KNN precomputed using dist² avoids sqrt in build. Zero-sqrt edge updates after reversal (interior edges reverse order). This enables 2-opt for N=200K within 1 second, whereas window 2-opt was infeasible for N>10K.
applicability_bounds: Holds for grid-distributed cities with uniform-ish density. TLE instability (~5-point drops on 2/6 runs) is environmental, not algorithmic — both baseline and treatment suffer identically.

statement: Both iter-1 and iter-2 TSP solutions exhibit ~5-point score drops on some judge runs due to TLE on large test cases. This is environmental (machine load), not algorithmic — both solutions drop identically. Reported scores should use non-TLE runs for algorithm comparison.
evidence: iteration-2: treatment TLE'd 2/6 runs (73.93 vs 78.93), baseline TLE'd 3/4 runs (73.29 vs 78.29)
mechanism: Judge enforces 2-second wall-clock limit per test case. Under machine load, solutions that use most of the time budget (1.7-1.9s) occasionally exceed 2s on the largest test cases, receiving zero score for those cases. The 5-point drop corresponds to ~1 large test case TLE.
applicability_bounds: Specific to local execution environment. Judge server may have more stable timing.

statement: For penalized TSP problem #44, grid nearest-neighbor construction dominates tour quality. The spatial grid with G=sqrt(N/2.5) cells per dimension achieves ~78.2/100 score for construction alone. Combined with candidate-list 2-opt + ILS, total reaches 78.93. Local search adds ~0.7 points.
regime: N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, cities sorted by x-coordinate
mechanism: Grid NN groups cities by spatial proximity in 2D. Finer grid (N/2.5 vs N/4) provides more precise neighbor lookup. Local search (candidate-list 2-opt + ILS) adds ~0.7 points by eliminating crossing edges and escaping local optima.
applicability_bounds: Finer grid (N/2.5) is optimal when KNN build time is budgeted; coarser grid (N/4) is safer if timing is tight.
